writeup: TIC 378434189 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.8113 days. The TESS photometry shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 5.96 percent dimming, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 96.2 using the box least-squares method. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location, with a peak difference-imaging signal-to-noise of 46.7 and a centroid offset of 1.3 arcseconds from the target. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine learning screening score of 0.37 indicates moderate confidence that this is a real stellar system rather than an artifact. No data quality issues were flagged during automated processing.
